subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what activity source, thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, and user-visible notification behavior should be accepted?
rationale: The remaining work changes recovery policy, config/default behavior, child-run mutation, and channel-visible failure handling for existing deployments, so source inspection cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Define Core Recovery Policy
options.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to session activity plus kill/reap work.

options.title: Prototype Default-Off
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in watchdog first, with focused source and live proof and no behavior change for existing installs until defaults are approved.

options.title: Defer Automatic Recovery
options.body: Rely on runTimeoutSeconds plus manual kill/reap and session-activity work for now, revisiting automatic intervention only with more production evidence.

recommendation.title: Define Core Recovery Policy
recommendation.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to session activity plus kill/reap work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for sessions_spawn, subagent config/docs, and adjacent registry behavior.
